newsitem.title: INDIA: Two killed in Kashmir blast, 39 wounded.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Kashmir blast, 39 wounded.

text.p: A bomb exploded at a bus stand in Kashmir on Wednesday, killing the man carrying the device and a bystander, Indian police said.
Thirty-nine people were wounded, 15 of them seriously, in the blast in Pulwama town, 32 km (20 miles) south of the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, Srinagar, they said.
"An explosive device being carried by a man went off in Pulwama bus stand where a large number of people were on the move," a police officer in Srinagar said.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have been killed in Jammu and Kashmir, mostly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state, since a separatist revolt erupted in 1990.
A defence spokesman said earlier on Wednesday that Indian soldiers killed nine guerrillas who had crossed the border from Pakistan into Kashmir.
The militants were killed overnight in a gun battle in Michil near the India-Pakistan border and about 85 km (55 miles) north of Srinagar.
